news.n_title: Dsouza? India's teqball star nears historic Asian Games medal
news.n_short_desc: Asian Games 2027: Quimcy Dsouza reached the women's singles semi-final after topping her group in teqball's Asian Games debut. The Indian is now one win away from a maiden medal for the country in the sport.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
Dsouza is one win away from securing India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in teqball after the 24-year-old topped her group in the sport’s Games debut in Nagoya on Friday. She fought back to beat Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto 10-12, 12-11, 13-11 before defeating Cambodia’s Koemyean Dy 12-9, 12-7.

ADS

Quimcy will face Indonesia’s Sumaya in the women’s singles semi-final on Saturday, with victory guaranteeing her a historic podium finish. If she loses, she will still have a shot at bronze against the loser of the other semi-final between Myanmar’s Wai Khin Hin and Lebanon’s Kamar Dandal.

Her run has become even more significant after India’s other teqball campaign ended in the men’s doubles. Declan Marshall Gonsalves and Mohamed Anas Imran Beg lost both their Group B matches, going down 0-2 to Vietnam and South Korea, and were eliminated before the quarter-finals. Beg, however, remains in contention alongside Quimcy in the mixed doubles.

For someone now on the verge of an Asian Games medal, Quimcy’s route to the sport has been anything but conventional. A former football and athletics competitor, the Mumbai-born athlete only took up teqball in 2022 and has since grown into one of India’s leading players.

news.n_title: No foreign influence: Govt hits back at 'external pressure' charge on UPI fee
news.n_short_desc: The government has rejected the opposition's charge that the introduction of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI payments was intended to benefit American card companies.

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
The Centre on Wednesday rejected claims that the introduction of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI payments was driven by foreign influence, after the opposition alleged that the move was aimed at appeasing US President Donald Trump. Clearing the air over the allegations, the Finance Ministry said India's UPI policy decisions were made "independently", and it would continue to remain free for consumers.

ADS

WHAT IS THE NEW UPI MDR FEE?

From October 15, UPI transactions over Rs 2,000 will attract an MDR fee of 0.4%. However, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) said this would be paid by merchants, and consumers won't be affected.

For instance, a merchant will pay Rs 40 when it receives a UPI payment of Rs 10,000. A shopkeeper or an entity receiving more than Rs 1 lakh per month from customers through UPI is categorised as a merchant.

The MDR fee, however, has been capped at Rs 300 per transaction.

Amid criticism from the opposition, which has sought its rollback, the Centre reiterated that "person-to-person transfers" would always remain free.

Separately, the Finance Ministry said banks have been advised to ensure merchants do not pass on the cost to customers. "Sending money to friends, paying at shops, or scanning a QR code - all remain without charges," the statement said

n_offline_data.no_desc_withouthtml:
India's men's cricket team will begin its Asian Games campaign in Japan on September 28, with the Shreyas Iyer-led side entering the competition directly in the quarter-finals. The women's team, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, will begin its campaign against Japan on September 18.

ADS

Both Indian teams are seeded and will start their campaigns from the quarter-final stage. They will go into the competition as firm favourites for the gold medal after sweeping the cricket events at the previous edition in Hangzhou.

In the men's competition, 10 teams will take part, with India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka receiving direct entry into the quarter-finals. India have been placed in Quarter-final 2, while Pakistan will feature in Quarter-final 1.

India will face the second-placed team from Group A, which comprises Afghanistan, Japan and Nepal. Pakistan, meanwhile, will take on the runners-up from Group B, featuring Hong Kong, China, Malaysia and Oman.

The remaining six teams will have to come through the group stage to reach the last eight. The top two teams from each group will progress to the quarter-finals.

The semi-final draw has kept India and Pakistan on opposite sides of the bracket. The winner of Quarter-final 1 will face the winner of Quarter-final 3, while the winner of Quarter-final 2 will take on the winner of Quarter-final 4. The semi-finals are scheduled for October 1.

As a result, India and Pakistan cannot meet in the semi-finals. If both teams win their respective quarter-finals and then make it through the semi-finals, they can meet only in the gold-medal match on October 3. If they lose in the semi-finals, they could face each other in the bronze-medal play-off on the same day.

The women's competition will get underway earlier, with India taking on Japan on September 18. The women's final is scheduled for September 22, while the men's summit clash will be played on October 3.

India's women's team will be looking to defend the gold medal it won in Hangzhou, while the men will aim to repeat the success of the previous edition. With both teams entering at the quarter-final stage, India will be among the leading contenders for gold in both competitions.

news.n_short_desc: Neeraj Chopra produced a season-best 88.05m throw to finish second at the Lausanne Diamond League. The performance offers timely momentum as he builds towards defending his Asian Games title next month.
